section_summary: The section closes a preliminary Post Office Inspector's report on Yamamoto, alleging a prior U.S. tax conviction, deportation to Japan, and connections to gambling, murder, and bail for Japanese defendants on the Pacific Coast. It then contains a January 1939 report to the State Department describing George Jenison's account of approaches by Takahashi for technical information about poison gas, aircraft materials, molybdenum, and other metals, together with an invitation to work in Japan.

subfiles.title: Continuation of preliminary report on Yamamoto
subfiles.from: S. H. Morse, Post Office Inspector
subfiles.about: The report relays allegations concerning Yamamoto's criminal history, deportation, gambling operations, and financial assistance to Japanese murder defendants in California.
subfiles.summary: Concluding page: Yamamoto served three months for tax violations, paid $3,000 and was deported; he reportedly ran gambling operations on the Pacific Coast and posted bail for suspects in a murder; claims unverified.

subfiles.title: Report of interview with George Jenison concerning Takahashi
subfiles.from: C. T. Hansen, Inspector in Charge, Post Office Department, Denver
subfiles.to: R. C. Bannerman, Chief Special Agent, Department of State
subfiles.about: Hansen reports Jenison's claim that Takahashi sought sensitive scientific and military-related information and tried to recruit him to go to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Postal inspectors interviewed George Jenison January 17, 1939: Takahashi asked about poison gases and metals, invited him to Japan, and was an official of the Japanese government; Jenison refused and urged surveillance.
